elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer against covered claims.
elements.evidence: Section 9A.1 expressly requires HDI to defend the Company.

elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer's affiliates against covered claims.
elements.evidence: Section 9A.1 extends HDI's defense obligation to the Company's affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer against covered claims.
elements.evidence: Section 9A.1 expressly requires HDI to indemnify the Company for claims and resulting losses.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer's affiliates against covered claims.
elements.evidence: Section 9A.1 expressly extends HDI's indemnification obligation to the Company's affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor's defense and indemnity must apply to third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Section 9A.1 applies to “any third-party claim.”

elements.element: Covered claims must include allegations that the services or deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Section 9A.1(a) covers allegations that the Site, Services, software, tools, technology, or other HDI deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right.

elements.element: Covered claims must include claims arising from Vendor's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Section 9A.1(b) covers claims arising from HDI's breach of applicable law.

elements.element: Covered claims must include data breaches caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Section 9A.1(c) covers unauthorized access to or disclosure of Content, Confidential Information, or customer data caused by HDI.

elements.element: Covered claims must include claims arising from Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Section 9A.1(d) expressly covers HDI's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must require Customer to notify Vendor of the claim.
elements.evidence: Section 9A.1 conditions HDI's obligations on the Company promptly notifying HDI of the claim.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must permit Vendor to control the defense and settlement.
elements.evidence: Section 9A.1 permits HDI to control the defense and settlement, subject to Company consent for settlements imposing liability, obligations, or admissions on the Company.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must require Customer to provide reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: Section 9A.1 requires reasonable cooperation from the Company at HDI's expense.

elements.element: Customer must indemnify Vendor for third-party claims arising from Customer-provided content.
elements.evidence: Section 9A.2 requires the Company to indemnify HDI for third-party claims arising from Content or Marks provided by the Company.

elements.element: Customer must indemnify Vendor for third-party claims arising from Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Section 9A.2 covers third-party claims arising from the Company's breach of applicable law.

elements.element: Customer's indemnity must not extend beyond Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Section 9A.2 contains no other trigger; its scope is confined to Company-provided Content or Marks and the Company's breach of applicable law.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer against third-party IP infringement or misappropriation claims relating to Vendor's services or deliverables.
elements.evidence: Section 9A.1(a) provides an IP indemnity for the Site, Services, software, tools, technology, and other HDI deliverables.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude claims caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: No exclusion for modifications made by the Company appears in Section 9A.1 or elsewhere in the rendered language.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude claims caused by combinations with items not supplied or approved by Vendor.
elements.evidence: No combination exclusion appears in the rendered language.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude claims resulting from Customer-provided specifications.
elements.evidence: The clause excludes claims arising from Company-provided Content or Marks, but it does not exclude claims resulting from compliance with Customer specifications.

elements.element: For a covered IP claim, Vendor must have or provide a remedy to procure Customer's continued right to use the affected item.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no procure-right remedy for an IP claim.

elements.element: For a covered IP claim, Vendor must have or provide a remedy to modify the affected item so it becomes non-infringing.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no modification remedy.

elements.element: For a covered IP claim, Vendor must have or provide a remedy to replace the affected item with a non-infringing alternative.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no replacement remedy.

elements.element: For a covered IP claim, Vendor must have or provide a refund remedy.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no refund remedy.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity liability must be subject to a super-cap equal to three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No liability cap or super-cap of three times annual fees appears in the rendered language.

result.reason: The operative language satisfies every preferred requirement, including the four Vendor indemnity triggers, affiliate protection, notice/control/cooperation mechanics, and the restricted reciprocal indemnity. The fallback is not satisfied because the usual modification, combination, and specification exclusions, all four IP remedies, and the 3× annual-fees super-cap are absent. The redline preserves unrelated terms and introduces no contradiction, but it is not strictly minimal because it adds a defense obligation for the Company, although the preferred position requires only a limited Customer indemnity. Drafting is generally strong, with minor placement and scope issues, including inserting Section 9A after Section 10.7 and subjecting indemnity survival to the existing two-year limit.
